query: The Lost-Property Box {The porter wants the lost-property box sorted before it starts to smell, and pays by the hour.|The lost-property box is full again, the porter says, mostly of the same gloves.|The porter slides the box across without a word. You know where the odd boot goes now.} Sort it quickly for the pay {Gloves, scarves, books and one boot, in piles by dusk. The porter pays and keeps the boot for himself.|You sort it in an hour. The porter pays for two, out of habit.|You sort it fast. The porter pays, and then tries the odd boot on again, hopefully.} Read what people lose {You learn who carries love letters and who never returns library books. The porter pays you less for taking so long.|You read the names in the books and the notes in the pockets, and put everything back exactly. A slow hour, and a useful one.|You know the castle by what it drops. The porter pays a little less, and you put the gossip away for later.}
